terrazzo.title: Terrazzo Flooring
terrazzo.lead: Durable and stylish, terrazzo flooring blends marble, quartz, and glass for timeless, low-maintenance elegance.
paras: Chips of marble, quartz and glass set into a binder, then ground and polished flat. The result is a seamless surface with genuine depth — and a service life measured in decades rather than years.

Terrazzo is poured in place, so it has no seams for dirt to collect in and no tiles to lift. Aggregate colour, chip size and divider strips are all specified per project, which makes it the system of choice when the floor is part of the architecture rather than a background to it.

Because the surface is ground and polished after curing, it can be restored decades later by grinding it back rather than replacing it. That is what keeps terrazzo in service in transit halls, civic buildings and schools long after other finishes have been torn out twice.
Terrazzo finishing, grinding and polishing is core work for our crews — it's the discipline the company was built on.

vct.title: VCT Flooring
vct.lead: Vinyl Composition Tile offers affordable, resilient flooring ideal for high-traffic commercial and institutional spaces.
paras: Vinyl Composition Tile is the workhorse of institutional flooring: inexpensive per square foot, available in a wide colour range, and replaceable one tile at a time.

VCT arrives as rigid tiles that are adhered to a prepared subfloor. Because the format is modular, a damaged area can be lifted and replaced without touching the surrounding floor — a meaningful advantage in buildings that stay open while repairs happen.

The trade-off is maintenance: VCT expects a periodic strip-and-wax cycle to keep its finish. Where a facility has the cleaning programme to support that, it delivers the lowest installed cost of any system we lay.
Colour can be laid out in patterns, borders and wayfinding lines, which is why it remains standard in schools, clinics and back-of-house areas.

carpet-tile.title: Carpet Tile Flooring
carpet-tile.lead: Modular carpet that installs fast, absorbs sound, and lets you replace damaged sections one tile at a time.
paras: Modular carpet that installs fast, absorbs sound, and lets you replace the worn squares instead of the whole floor.

Carpet tile solves the two problems broadloom carpet has in commercial space: waste during installation, and total replacement when one area wears out. Tiles are laid from the centre outward and cut only at the perimeter, and stock can be held back for future repairs.

Acoustically it is the quietest option we install — worth specifying in open-plan offices and anywhere speech privacy matters. It is also the warmest underfoot, which changes how a space feels more than most people expect.
Patterned and plank formats allow zoning and wayfinding without changing material, and tiles can be rotated during their life to even out wear.

rubber.title: Rubber Flooring
rubber.lead: Dense, resilient sheet and tile that absorbs impact, grips underfoot wet or dry, and stands up to heavy daily abuse.
paras: Dense, resilient sheet and tile that absorbs impact, grips underfoot when wet, and shrugs off dropped weight.

Rubber is specified where the floor takes punishment: weight rooms, sports halls, plant rooms and circulation routes that see trolleys and equipment all day. Its resilience protects both the substrate below and the equipment dropped on it.

Slip resistance holds up in wet conditions better than most hard surfaces, which is why it appears around changing rooms and entrances. It needs no wax — routine cleaning is enough to maintain the finish, which lowers lifetime cost against systems that require a polish cycle.
Available in sheet for a near-seamless field, or interlocking tile where sections may need lifting for access.

sheet-vinyl.title: Sheet Vinyl Flooring
sheet-vinyl.lead: Wide-roll vinyl with heat-welded seams, producing a continuous waterproof surface designed for sterile and high-spill environments.
paras: Wide-roll vinyl with heat-welded seams, producing a continuous waterproof surface that can be coved up the wall.

Where hygiene governs the specification, sheet vinyl is usually the answer. Seams are heat-welded rather than butted, and the material can be coved at the wall junction to remove the dirt-trapping corner entirely — giving a floor that can genuinely be washed down.
That makes it standard in clinical areas, food preparation spaces, laboratories and washrooms. Slip-resistant grades are available where water is expected underfoot.
Modern print and wear layers cover a wide design range, including convincing wood and stone visuals, without giving up the continuous waterproof surface.

epoxy.title: Epoxy Flooring
epoxy.lead: A liquid-applied resin system that cures into a hard, jointless, chemically resistant floor for industrial and commercial environments.
paras: A liquid-applied resin system that cures into a hard, jointless, chemically resistant surface bonded directly to the slab.

Epoxy is applied as a liquid and cures in place, so it follows falls, forms coves and leaves no joints. Bonded to a properly prepared slab it produces a floor that resists oils, solvents and cleaning chemicals that would attack most other finishes.

Build-up can be varied from a thin roller-applied coating to a heavy-duty screed, depending on whether the floor faces foot traffic, forklifts or thermal shock. Anti-slip aggregate can be broadcast into the surface where required, and line marking is applied as part of the system.
Slab preparation decides whether an epoxy floor lasts. Mechanical grinding and moisture testing before any resin goes down is not an optional extra — it's the job.
